Accumulated knowledge from decompilation attempts. Each insight should help
future attempts match MWCC output more reliably. Query without reading the
whole file: `patterns.py query --grep <word>`.

## Compiler: MWCC 2.0/sp2p2

### Target and flags  <!-- id: mwcc-flags -->

- Target: ARM946E-S (ARMv5TE), primarily Thumb mode
- Flags: `-O4,p -enum int -lang c99 -char signed -inline on,noauto -interworking`
- `-O4,p` means level 4 optimization with peephole; this aggressively reorders code
- `-inline on,noauto` means inlining is allowed but only when explicitly requested (via `inline` keyword or `__attribute__((always_inline))`)

### MWCC errors on int->enum implicit conversion (use named enum constants)  <!-- id: int-to-enum-strict -->

MWCC -W error treats passing an int literal to an enum-typed parameter as an illegal implicit conversion (e.g. Heap_Create(3, 0x30, ...) where params are enum HeapID -> illegal implicit conversion from int to HeapID). Fix: use the named enum constant (HEAP_ID_3, HEAP_ID_48) or an explicit (enum X) cast. Codegen is identical (mov #imm), so this is purely about getting it to compile. The enum HEAP_ID_<N> names are sequential = value N.

### x >> n on a u8/u16 emits asr (signed); retail lsr means the operand is u32/unsigned  <!-- id: u8-u16-rshift-promotes-signed-asr -->

A right shift `x >> n` where x is u8 or u16 promotes x to signed int per C integer promotion, so MWCC emits an arithmetic shift (asr). If the asm shows a logical/unsigned shift (lsr) at that spot, the original operand was an unsigned type that does NOT promote to signed — i.e. u32 (or unsigned int). Fix: declare/cast the operand as u32 (e.g. change a derived param type from u8 to u32, or write ((u32)x >> n)). Left shifts (<<) are unaffected (lsl either way). Seen in unk_0205BFF0.c sub_0205C0A0: `b >> 1` with b as u8 emitted `asr r0,r1,#1` (0x1048); retail had `lsr r0,r1,#1` (0x0848); changing b to u32 fixed it. Note u16 also promotes to signed int, so u16 does NOT give lsr — only u32/unsigned does.

## General Codegen

### Register allocation follows declaration order  <!-- id: regalloc-order -->

- MWCC allocates registers in order: r0-r3 for arguments, r4-r7 for locals (Thumb), r4-r11 for locals (ARM); arguments beyond 4 on the stack; return values in r0 (r0-r1 for 64-bit).
- MWCC assigns callee-saved registers based on variable declaration order in the function. Reordering declarations can swap registers and break matching.
- When the asm uses r6 for variable A and r7 for variable B, try declaring B before A (MWCC sometimes allocates in reverse declaration order).
- Moving a declaration from block scope to function scope changes register lifetime and can affect allocation — match the original variable scoping as closely as C89 allows.
- Functions with many locals: register pressure causes spills to stack in specific order; declaration order is load-bearing.

### Stack frame shape  <!-- id: stack-frame -->

- `push {r4-r7, lr}` / `pop {r4-r7, pc}` is typical Thumb prologue/epilogue.
- `sub sp, #N` for local variables; `add sp, #N` before return; stack variables accessed via `sp + offset`.

### Control flow lowering  <!-- id: control-flow -->

- `if/else` compiles to `cmp + bCC`; `switch` compiles to branch table or cascading compares depending on density.
- Loops compile test-at-top or test-at-bottom; MWCC often hoists loop-invariant loads outside the loop body.
- MWCC sometimes emits `bx` to switch between ARM/Thumb for interworking.

### Data access shapes  <!-- id: data-access -->

- Global data accessed via `ldr rN, =address` (literal pool).
- Struct member access: `ldr rN, [rBase, #offset]`; array access: index * element_size + base.
- Load width reveals the type: `ldrb`=u8, `ldrh`=u16, `ldrsh`=s16, `ldrsb`=s8, `ldr`=u32/pointer.

### Common MWCC idioms  <!-- id: mwcc-idioms -->

- `mov r0, #0` / `mov r0, #1` for FALSE/TRUE returns.
- `add rN, rM, #0` is `mov rN, rM` in Thumb; `lsl r0, r0, #0` is a NOP MWCC sometimes emits.

### Cast a signed param to unsigned to force bhs/blo branches  <!-- id: cast-unsigned-for-branch -->

When a function param is declared signed (e.g. int) per its fixed header, but the asm compares it with an UNSIGNED branch (bhs/blo/bhi/bls) against a u16 table value, force the comparison unsigned by casting at the comparison site: if ((u32)mapsec < p[1]). The cast is free (no instruction) and flips bge/blt -> bhs/blo. A signed int vs u16 promotes both to int and yields signed branches, so the cast is required. Distinguish per-comparison: the loop counter (int i) can stay signed (blt) in the same function while the value comparison is unsigned.

### Raw pointer casts to magic hardware addresses match byte-for-byte  <!-- id: raw-addr-cast-match -->

For files touching fixed DS addresses (0x027FFxxx ROM-header/system-work region), *(u32 *)0xADDR (direct) gives ldr =0xADDR; ldr [r0]; *(u32 *)((u8 *)BASE + off) gives ldr =BASE (loaded once, reused); ldr [rN,#off]. The SAME address can appear both ways in one function (flag check *(u32*)0x027FF00C and header->gamecode at base 0x027FF000 +0xC) -> use both forms. Named HW_ consts (HW_ROM_HEADER_BUF, HW_CARD_ROM_HEADER, HW_CARD_ROM_HEADER_SIZE) match identically to raw literals. A stack struct of size 0xN (FSFile=0x48) gives sub sp,#0xN; read field via *(u32*)((u8*)&s+off).

### Declaration order controls r2/r3 allocation for same-lifetime locals  <!-- id: decl-order-regalloc -->

When two locals share a live range and compete for low Thumb registers (r2/r3), MWCC -O4,p assigns the FIRST-DECLARED variable to the LOWER register. If objdiff shows two functions identical except a consistent r2<->r3 (or rN<->rM) swap, reorder the local declarations to flip the allocation. Example: unk_02017FAC sub_02017FAC needed int i=0 declared before const u16 *p=table so i->r2 (counter/return reg) and p->r3 (walked pointer), matching asm.

### A u16 value loaded via ldrh compares unsigned (bcc/blo) against a constant without a cast  <!-- id: u16-from-ldrh-unsigned-branch -->

When a function param/value is u16 and is read via ldrh (zero-extended), a bounds check like GF_ASSERT(index < 4) compiles to cmp + bcc (unsigned blo) WITHOUT needing an explicit (u32) cast — MWCC knows the ldrh-zero-extended value is non-negative and emits the unsigned branch. This is distinct from the signed-int-vs-u16 case (cast-unsigned-for-branch) where a value already widened to int needs an explicit (u32) cast to flip bge/blt to bhs/blo. Rule of thumb: keep the param u16 (matches the ldrh) and write the plain comparison; only add the (u32) cast when the value is int-typed. Example: overlay_80_02239AF8 ov80_02239AF8 (u16 index).

### Shared store + return as the function fall-off block: hoist value to a temp and store AFTER the switch  <!-- id: shared-store-return-as-fall-off-block -->

When several switch cases each compute a new value, store it to a struct field, and return the same code, MWCC in the retail build often emits ONE shared store+return block as the function LAST/fall-off block (both if/else arms `b` to it), with the cold `default: return 1;` laid out immediately BEFORE it. Three wrong C shapes: (1) store+return inside each case duplicates the store; (2) `break` with the store still in the case body splits the store into its own block plus an extra `b`; (3) `return 0` inside the last case makes MWCC place the cold default block AFTER the return-0 block (wrong order). RIGHT shape: hoist the value to a function-scope temp (`int newState;`), assign it in each arm, then `break`; do the shared store (`st->field = newState;`) and `return 0;` AFTER the switch as the trailing statements. MWCC then merges them into a single fall-off block (`strb; movs r0,#0; add sp; pop`) reached by branches, and places the cold `default: return 1` just before it. Note: `add sp,#N` lands at the END of the last/fall-off block but at the START of a non-last branched return block. Seen in overlay_80_02239BF0.c (ov80_02239C80 state-machine tail). Diagnose: function body matches byte-for-byte except the last ~14 bytes; objdiff shows a SIZE mismatch (inline-jumptable miscount masks it) — disassemble both .o with arm-none-eabi-objdump and compare the tail block order + add-sp placement.

## Matching Tricks

### Small source changes that move codegen  <!-- id: decl-order-tricks -->

- Variable declaration order affects register allocation.
- `u32` vs `int` can change sign-extension instructions; `size / 2` vs `size >> 1` can differ at -O4 — try both.
- Ternary `a ? b : c` can produce different code than `if/else`.
- Assigning to a temp variable vs direct use changes register lifetimes.
- `NELEMS(array)` (sizeof/sizeof) matches constant folding.
- Casting to `(void)` suppresses warnings without changing codegen.

### u16 parameter narrowing tells you the original type  <!-- id: param-narrowing -->

- A `u16` param makes MWCC insert `lsls rN,rN,#16; lsrs rN,rN,#16` narrowing at function entry; `int` params skip it. No narrowing at entry but `ldrh` use inside → the original param was likely `int` (or the caller's header said `int`).
- Calling a `u16`-declared function with an `int` argument inserts narrowing at the call site. No narrowing in the asm → the callee's prototype used `int`.
- Tail-call wrappers must forward argument types exactly — changing `int` → `u16` inserts unwanted narrowing before the tail call.

### Switch case bodies are emitted in source order  <!-- id: switch-case-source-order -->

MWCC emits switch case code blocks in **source order**, not numeric order. Jump-table entries are always numeric, but the code they point to follows source layout — reorder the C cases to match the asm's block order. Fall-through patterns also depend on case order.

### Branch polarity reveals || vs &&  <!-- id: branch-or-vs-and -->

- `if (a || b) { body }` → `cmp a; bne body; cmp b; beq skip`
- `if (a && b) { body }` → `cmp a; beq skip; cmp b; beq skip`
The branch direction (beq vs bne after comparisons) tells you which logical operator was used; getting it wrong produces same-size code with different branch instructions.

### GF_ASSERT and if/else direction  <!-- id: gf-assert-direction -->

`GF_ASSERT(cond)` expands to `if (!cond) GF_AssertFail()` — the assert-fail path is the else branch. `cmp; beq over_assert; bl AssertFail` corresponds to `if (flag == 0) { GF_AssertFail(); }`, not `GF_ASSERT(flag != 0)` — both are logically equivalent but produce different branch polarity. Swapping which path comes first changes encoding.

### lsls/lsrs pairs are bitfield extractions  <!-- id: bitfield-lsls-lsrs -->

`lsls rN,rN,#K; lsrs rN,rN,#K` extracts the low (32-K) bits. Use a bitfield struct member (e.g. `u32 fileId : 24`) rather than `& 0x00FFFFFF` — the mask may generate `ldr + and` with a literal-pool constant instead. `(x << 8) >> 8` can also produce the pattern but may not match. Bit packing order is compiler-specific: use bitfield structs, not masks.

### Loop shape selection  <!-- id: loop-shapes -->

- `for (i = 0; i < N; i++)` may compile as test-at-bottom (do/while shape) at -O4; if the count can be zero there's an early-exit check.
- Byte-clearing loops (`strb; adds; subs; bne`) need C that puts decrement+branch at the bottom: `do { } while (--n)` vs `while (n != 0) { n--; }` produce different patterns — trial and error is sometimes required.

### cmp r4 vs cmp r0 after a parameter copy (copy propagation)  <!-- id: param-copyprop-cmp -->

When a parameter (r0) is copied to a callee-saved register (`adds r4, r0, #0`), MWCC copy-propagates: comparisons on the copy are substituted back to r0. `adds r4,r0,#0; cmp r4,#N` ONLY occurs when r0 is a **function return value** saved before a later call would clobber it. If the target asm shows the cmp-on-copy pattern at function entry with no preceding bl, pure C cannot produce it — use NONMATCHING (seen in unk_0200B150.s OamManager_Create).

### Other known difficult patterns  <!-- id: misc-difficult-patterns -->

- Nested struct initialization may need exact field ordering to match.
- Inline functions from headers must match exactly as the compiler would expand them (e.g. MI_CpuClearFast/MI_CpuCopyFast wrappers inline into MIi_* tail calls — call the wrapper, not MIi_* directly).
- Functions with a `_` prefix are often compiler-generated or SDK functions (`_s32_div_f`).

### Force a jump table: list ALL dense cases explicitly (sparse -> if-else)  <!-- id: switch-jumptable-density -->

When the asm uses a Thumb jump table (cmp rN,#max; bhi default; add rN,rN; add rN,pc; ldrh [rN,#6]; add pc,rN; then a halfword offset table), the C switch must cover the range 0..max DENSELY. Listing only the cases with bodies (e.g. case 1, case 4) plus default makes MWCC emit an if-else comparison chain instead (shorter, wrong). Fix: list EVERY case 0..max explicitly, giving the empty ones a bare break (case 0: break; case 2: break; ...). MWCC then sees a dense 0..max switch and emits the jump table. Body blocks are emitted in source order, so order the non-empty cases to match the asm block layout. Diagnose via objdiff --disasm (if-else cmp chain vs add pc,rN). Note: objdiff may report a spurious SIZE diff on a matching jump-table function because it disassembles the data-region table as code ($d/$t mapping symbols differ) — confirm with chiri pkg -- compare.

### Hoist a reused computed size into a local so it lives in a callee-saved register  <!-- id: hoist-size-local-callee-saved -->

When the asm computes a value once (e.g. count*4 via a single lsls) and keeps it in a callee-saved register (r4-r7) across multiple calls that reuse it (Heap_Alloc size AND FS_ReadFile len), the source declared an explicit local for it. Recomputing inline (header.a*4 written at each Heap_Alloc/FS_ReadFile site) makes MWCC reload+recompute each time -> function grows (asm 164B, naive C 170B) and the value never occupies a persistent callee-saved reg. Fix: u32 sizeA = header.a*4; pass sizeA to both the alloc and the read. Diagnose via objdiff size diff + extra ldrh/lsls before each use. Reg pick (r6 vs r4) follows usual decl-order/param-reuse: a dead param register (path in r4) is reused for the later-born size local. Example: overlay_01_021EA6C4 ov01_021EA73C.

### Force an unsigned loop branch (bcc/blo) with a 2u literal, keeping the counter int  <!-- id: unsigned-literal-branch-no-regshuffle -->

When a loop counter is int but the asm uses an UNSIGNED branch (bcc/blo) for its bound check (cmp #N; bcc), changing the counter type to u32 fixes the branch BUT can shuffle the whole functions register allocation (u32 changes how MWCC allocates the counter and dependent temps). Instead keep the counter as int and make ONLY the comparison unsigned with an unsigned literal: for (i = 0; i < 2u; i++). The int->unsigned promotion at the compare site flips blt->bcc with zero extra instructions and leaves register allocation identical to the int version. Use this when the int version matched everything EXCEPT signed-vs-unsigned loop branches. Example: overlay_80_022384D8 ov80_0223857C (2x2 fill loops).

### Force MWCC to batch field loads before arithmetic with explicit operand locals in load order  <!-- id: explicit-operand-locals-force-load-batching -->

When a function reads several struct fields then does arithmetic on them (e.g. a point-in-rect test computing right=x+width-1, bottom=y+height-1), MWCC -O4,p's scheduler chooses whether to BATCH all the loads up front or INTERLEAVE load-compute-load-compute. Writing `int right = zone->x + zone->width - 1; int bottom = zone->y + zone->height - 1;` (named result locals, or fully-inline exprs) made MWCC compute right completely (load x, load width, add, sub) BEFORE loading y/height -> a same-SIZE-but-byte-different mismatch plus a consistent rN<->rM swap (right/y landed in swapped registers). The original loaded ALL four fields first (x, width, y, height) then did both adds then both subs. Fix: introduce one explicit local PER OPERAND, declared in the asm's load order, assigned before any use: `int x=zone->x; int width=zone->width; int y=zone->y; int height=zone->height; int right=x+width-1; int bottom=y+height-1;`. The upfront assignments make the scheduler emit the 4 loads consecutively (decl order = load order x,width,y,height) and the operand-reuse registers fall out exactly (x=r5, right=r3 reusing width's reg, y=r4, bottom=r2 reusing height's reg). Diagnose via objdiff --disasm: identical instructions/branches, only load positions + 2 cmp operand regs differ. Example: overlay_01_021FB368 ov01_021FB368 (static rect-contains helper).

### Chained field assignment stores RIGHT-first; add a local to stop a struct-store alias reload  <!-- id: chained-assign-store-order-and-alias-reload -->

Two related store/CSE tricks seen in overlay_01_021FCD2C ov01_021FCD2C. (1) STORE ORDER of a chained assignment a = b = expr: MWCC evaluates expr once, assigns to the RIGHTMOST target first, then propagates left. So `work->unk10 = work->unk20 = X;` stores unk20 THEN unk10. If the asm stores the lower offset first (str r0,[r4,#0x10] then str r0,[r4,#0x20]), you must write the chain the other way: `work->unk20 = work->unk10 = X;` (rightmost = unk10 stored first, then unk20). Diagnose via objdiff --disasm: two adjacent str of the same reg with swapped offsets. (2) ALIAS RELOAD: `work->ptrField = obj->field; ... f(obj->field);` made MWCC RELOAD obj->field for the call because the intervening store to work->ptrField may alias obj->field (it cannot prove work != obj) -> an extra ldr (SIZE +2). The asm loaded obj->field ONCE into a reg, stored it, and reused that reg for the call. Fix: hoist into an explicit local: `Camera *camera = obj->field; work->ptrField = camera; f(camera);` -> single load, register reused, no reload. The local lives in a caller-saved reg (dies after the call) so it adds no push.

### Stack-slot OFFSET assignment is reverse declaration order (first-declared = highest sp+offset)  <!-- id: stack-slot-reverse-decl-order -->

Distinct from register-allocation decl-order tricks: when a function has MULTIPLE stack-resident locals (arrays or structs that must live at sp+offset, i.e. their address is taken or they're too big for a reg), MWCC -O4,p assigns the stack SLOTS in REVERSE declaration order — the FIRST-declared local gets the HIGHEST sp offset, the LAST-declared gets the lowest. Diagnose via objdiff --disasm: same instructions but `add rN, sp, #X` / `str rN, [sp,#X]` offsets are permuted between two equal-size stack locals. Fix: reorder the C declarations so the wanted layout falls out. Examples from unk_0201F990: (a) sub_0201F990 needed `s16 box[6]; VecFx32 trans; VecFx32 scale;` in that order to get scale@sp+0x10, trans@sp+0x1c, box@sp+0x28 (box first-declared -> highest). (b) sub_0201FAC8 needed `int result; u32 polyAttr; u32 begin;` to get result@sp+8 (highest), polyAttr@sp+4, begin@sp+0. Scalars that stay in registers (pointers, ints used immediately) do NOT participate — only the spilled/addressed locals do. Related but separate from [[decl-order-regalloc]] and [[regalloc-order]] which govern which REGISTER, not which stack offset.

### Reassign a dead parameter in-place to reuse its register and steer which local spills  <!-- id: reassign-dead-param-to-steer-spill -->

When several values must survive a sequence of calls and there are more survivors than callee-saved registers, MWCC -O4,p must spill some. If objdiff shows the SAME instructions but a DIFFERENT value spilled (e.g. asm computes `subs r5,r6,r5` keeping structSize in extraSize's register and spills tableSize, while your C spills structSize and keeps tableSize in a reg -> a ~2-byte size delta), steer the allocator by REUSING a now-dead parameter's storage: write `extraSize = heapSize - extraSize;` instead of introducing a fresh `u32 structSize = heapSize - extraSize;`. The in-place reassignment makes MWCC reuse extraSize's callee-saved register for the new value (matching the asm's in-place `subs`), freeing the allocator to spill the other competing long-lived local instead. Seen in overlay_01_021FC4C4 ov01_021FC4C4 ctor. Related to [[decl-order-regalloc]] but the lever here is operand identity (reuse vs new variable), not declaration order.

### Cast index to (u32) in a GF_ASSERT range check to get the asm's unsigned (bcc/blo) compare  <!-- id: unsigned-cast-range-assert -->

Range-check asserts like `GF_ASSERT(idx < N)` (e.g. before a table lookup) compile to a SIGNED compare (cmp; blt/bge) when idx is `int`, but MWCC's array-bounds idiom in the retail code uses an UNSIGNED compare (cmp rN,#N; bcc/blo). objdiff shows a single conditional-branch opcode diff: asm `bcc/blo` (0xd3.. / unsigned-lower) vs C `blt` (0xdb.. / signed-less). Fix: cast the index to unsigned in the assert -> `GF_ASSERT((u32)idx < N);` -> emits cmp; bcc. The table index access itself (table[idx]) is unaffected by the cast. Seen across the lookup fns of unk_02077678 (sub_02077678/0207769C/02077800/02077818). Header may force the param to stay `int`, so cast at the comparison rather than changing the param type.

### Don't cache base->ptr in a local when the asm RELOADS it across calls (inverse of hoist-size-local)  <!-- id: no-cache-reloaded-pointer-across-calls -->

Counterpart to [[hoist-size-local-callee-saved]]. When a function holds a base pointer (e.g. fieldSystem in r4) and repeatedly dereferences base->ptr->field across several bl calls, MWCC RELOADS base->ptr after each call because a call may invalidate that memory (it can't prove base->ptr is unchanged). The original source therefore accessed base->ptr->field INLINE each time. Introducing a readability local `T *p = base->ptr;` breaks the match: a local is NOT invalidated by calls, so MWCC keeps it live in a CALLEE-SAVED register across the whole function, which (a) consumes an extra callee-saved reg and (b) WIDENS the push/pop (e.g. asm `push {r4,lr}` becomes C `push {r3,r4,r5,lr}`) — and the base pointer it displaces gets its own reg too. Diagnose via objdiff: many 'real byte diffs' that are actually just the wider push/pop + shifted reg numbers, and a SIZE delta of a few bytes. Fix: delete the local, write base->ptr->field inline at every use; CSE still collapses multiple derefs WITHIN a call-free span into one load (matching the asm's per-region single reload). Seen in overlay_01_021F3D38.c (ov01_021F3E10, ov01_021F3E4C: fieldSystem->unk68 reloaded 2-3x across BgSetPos/sub_0205B63C/sub_0205B6A0 calls). Contrast: cache the pointer in a local ONLY when the asm keeps it in a callee-saved reg across calls (D98 in the same file DOES cache fieldSystem->unk68 because fieldSystem itself is dead after the first load).

## IPA (-ipa file) Behavior

### Shared-header signatures are load-bearing across compilation units  <!-- id: ipa-shared-headers -->

MWCC `-ipa file` analyzes at file scope: changing a function's return or parameter types in a shared header causes cascading codegen changes in ALL functions in any compilation unit that calls it — even callers that discard the return value. If matched file A.c includes header H.h, you cannot change any declaration in H.h that A.c uses (even `void PlayBGM(u16)` → `BOOL PlayBGM(u16)`) without risking A.c's match. Workarounds: decompile header-sharing files as a group (sound.h family), fix all signatures in one coordinated commit, or NONMATCHING the conflicting functions.

### Non-static does NOT prevent IPA  <!-- id: ipa-static-no-escape -->

Making functions non-static does **not** stop `-ipa file` from optimizing across them — IPA analyzes all bodies in the compilation unit regardless of linkage. The objdump symbol table showing 'g' (global) on asm objects just means the assembler defaults labels to global, not that the original C was non-static. static vs non-static does slightly change register allocation in some cases, but never disables IPA CSE.

### IPA CSE caches repeated literal-pool addresses  <!-- id: ipa-cse-literal-pool -->

When a caller passes the same static-data address to a callee multiple times, MWCC may cache those addresses in callee-saved registers across calls, displacing other variables to the stack. The original binary may not do this if the original source structure prevented it (structure unknown). This is the blocking issue in unk_0200FA24 (BeginNormalPaletteFade calls sub_0200FE84 twice with identical pointer args).

### Frozen struct-only shared header: use a self-sufficient _internal.h in the defining TU  <!-- id: frozen-struct-header-split -->

When a save-chunk struct lives in a SHARED header frozen to struct-only (no global.h, no prototypes) so save_arrays.c stays byte-matched, that header cannot serve as the defining .c file main header: clang-format (IncludeBlocks Regroup + main-header-first) forces the same-stem header to the very top, ahead of global.h (priority 2), so u8/u16 are undefined when the struct parses. Fix: create include/<name>_internal.h that #includes global.h then re-declares the identical struct, and include THAT in the .c (its different stem dodges the main-header rule, so global.h sorts first). Leave the frozen header and save_arrays.c (DECL_CHUNK_EX) untouched; give public fns local forward declarations. Verify save_arrays.o is byte-identical (cmp) to confirm no IPA cascade. Example: unk_0202E41C.

### Use a private struct + cast when a shared param struct is incomplete (IPA-safe)  <!-- id: private-struct-for-incomplete-shared-type -->

When a function must allocate/fill a struct that an EXTERNAL matched function takes by pointer (e.g. PokeathlonCourse_LaunchApp(.., PokeathlonCourseArgs*)), but the shared struct in its header is incomplete/placeholder (filler bytes, more-fields-to-discover) and is included by other already-matched files: do NOT edit the shared header to name the fields (recompiles those TUs -> IPA cascade risk). Instead define a fully-typed PRIVATE struct in your .c with the exact byte layout you need and cast to the real type only at the external call: PokeathlonCourse_LaunchApp(fs, (PokeathlonCourseArgs *)work->app). sizeof(private)==sizeof(real) so the alloc size literal matches; field offsets you control reproduce the exact ldrb/ldrh/strb. Zero shared-header change = zero IPA risk. Example: unk_02095DF4 sub_02095E30.

### Frozen prototype header (u32 sigs, no global.h) also needs the _internal.h split  <!-- id: frozen-prototype-header-split -->

Generalizes frozen-struct-header-split to plain PROTOTYPE headers. If include/<name>.h declares the module funcs (e.g. u32 ov01_xxx(u32,u32)) but does NOT include global.h (relies on callers including global.h first), and it is included by already-matched files: when YOU write src/<name>.c, clang-format IncludeBlocks=Regroup + main-header-first force the same-stem <name>.h to the very top, ABOVE global.h. u32 is then undefined while the header parses -> MWCC treats u32 as implicit int -> later types.h redeclares u32 as unsigned long -> error: identifier u32 redeclared / function has no prototype. Fix: do NOT include the same-stem header in the .c; create include/<name>_internal.h (different stem dodges the main-header sort, sorts AFTER global.h) that #includes global.h then declares the same prototypes; include THAT. Leave the frozen <name>.h untouched so the matched callers do not recompile. Example: overlay_01_021F467C.

### Local frozen extern when a callee's header narrowed its params (int->u16) after this caller was matched  <!-- id: frozen-callee-proto-for-narrowed-args -->

Split-header discipline applies to CALLEE prototypes too, not just shared struct headers. If a function was originally compiled with a wider arg type for a callee (e.g. int) and the callee's header was LATER refined to a narrow type (u16/u8/s16), including that refined header makes MWCC emit an integer-narrowing the original asm lacks: a u32/int value passed to a u16 param gets a `lsls rN,#16; lsrs rN,#16` (zero-extend) or `lsls;asrs` (sign) truncation at the call site. Diagnose via objdiff --disasm: extra lsl/lsr #16 pairs around a bl that the asm doesn't have. Fix: do NOT include the refined header; declare a local `extern <ret> Fn(... int a2, int a3 ...);` with the wider (matched) arg types so no narrowing is emitted. Only works if the refined header is not force-included (grep its includers first; global.h chain must not pull it). Seen in unk_02097BE0 calling LegendaryCinematic_LaunchApp (launch_application.h has u16 a2/a3; matched int). Contrast [[frozen-prototype-header-split]] (struct/decl header) — same principle, applied to an imported function signature. NB: MWCC DOES narrow u32->u16 for outgoing args (confirmed: unk_020551B8 Sound_SetSceneAndPlayBGM seqNo), so a missing truncation in asm means the param was wider at match time.

### Header declares a narrower return type than the field (u8 vs u32) -> MWCC masks; if asm does not mask, the real return type is the wider one — use split-header  <!-- id: narrow-return-type-masks-split-header -->

Symptom: a getter that just does `ldr r0,[p,#off]; bx lr` (no lsl/lsr/and mask) but the existing/public header declares it returning u8 (or u16). With that header, MWCC appends a truncation (`lsls r0,#24; lsrs r0,#24`) and the function is 4 bytes too big (objdiff SIZE 10 vs 14). The asm proves the real return type is u32/int (the value is returned full-width; any narrowing is the CALLERs job). Fix WITHOUT editing the shared header (it is frozen at the matching-time state its callers were built against — changing the return type would alter caller codegen and break their match / cascade via IPA): do NOT include that public header in the defining .c. Instead include the underlying data/struct header (here friend_group.h) and forward-declare the affected functions LOCALLY with the correct (wider) return type. Different TUs may legitimately see different return-type declarations for the same symbol in a matching decomp — the linker only matches by name. Seen in unk_0202C730.c: Save_FriendGroup_GetGroupId declared u8 in unk_0202C730.h (5 matched callers) but defined u32 locally to drop the mask. Verified: full ROM SHA1 still passes, callers unaffected.

## Data Sections

### Section ↔ C mapping  <!-- id: section-mapping -->

- `.rodata` = const arrays/tables (use `const`); `.data` = initialized mutable globals; `.bss` = zero-initialized globals.
- Global variable order matters: declarations must match the asm order, and `.rodata` array order must match the section layout (an all-functions-match file can still fail ROM SHA1 on rodata order — see unk_0201010C).
- `.balign 4, 0` pads to 4-byte boundary — use struct padding or explicit alignment.
- ARM is little-endian: `.byte 0x25, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00` = u32 `0x00000025`.

### Data-only files  <!-- id: data-only-files -->

Some asm files contain only `.rodata`/`.data` sections. They need C files with const (or non-const) arrays matching the exact byte layout:
```c
#include "global.h"

const u8 sDataTable[] = {
    0x25, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,
};
```

### BSS sizing with raw byte arrays  <!-- id: bss-sizing -->

When asm BSS symbol sizes don't match `sizeof(StructType)`, use a raw `u8 array[0xNN]` and cast at usage sites: `*(StructType *)array`. Multiple BSS variables become separate `.bss` sections in the object but the linker merges them — the total size must match.

### Contiguous data arrays accessed via base+offset  <!-- id: contiguous-arrays-base-offset -->

When multiple data labels are accessed from a common base pointer (e.g. `ldr r0, =_0210F64C; str r1, [r0, #0x10]` targeting `_0210F65C`), the labels are contiguous. Declare them as separate static arrays in order — MWCC lays them out contiguously. Stores use base symbol + offset while call arguments use the target symbol directly; both produce correct literal pools as long as the arrays are separate declarations (not one big array with #defines).

### Packed lookup tables (VALUE | (code<<N)) are bitfield structs; access via members emits the asm's shift extraction  <!-- id: packed-lookup-table-is-bitfield-struct -->

A rodata table whose entries are `KEY | (CODE << N)` (e.g. `SPECIES_X | (22<<10)`) and whose readers extract fields with SHIFT PAIRS (`lsl #(32-N); lsr #(32-N)` for the low field; `lsl #16; lsr #(16+N)` style for the high field) is, in the original source, an array of a BITFIELD struct: `typedef struct { u16 key : N; u16 code : (16-N); } E;` with initializers `{ KEY, CODE }`. Accessing `tbl[i].key` / `tbl[i].code` makes MWCC emit the exact shift-pair extraction. Writing it as `static const u16 tbl[]` + `(tbl[i] & MASK)` / `(tbl[i] >> N)` instead emits AND-with-a-loaded-mask-register and asr — which (a) differ instruction-for-instruction and (b) consume an extra register for the mask, forcing a callee-saved reg + push/pop (function SIZE grows). Seen in unk_020517A4 (_020FC3B4 species table, _020FC3CA trainerclass table; both `{u16 id:10; u16 param:6}`). Diagnose: objdiff shows asr/and+mask vs lsl/lsr pairs, often with a spurious push {..} the asm lacks.

## Recurring File/Module Patterns

### Task callback pattern (field system)  <!-- id: task-callback-pattern -->

1. A public `sub_XXXX` allocates a work struct via `Heap_AllocAtEnd`, fills it, calls `TaskManager_Call(man, callback, env)`.
2. A static callback uses `TaskManager_GetFieldSystem` + `TaskManager_GetEnvironment`, implements a state machine (switch on `env->state`), returns TRUE when done after `Heap_Free`.
- The callback is referenced by literal pool (`_XXXX: .word sub_YYYY`) in the caller.
- Work struct fields can be inferred from how the caller stores arguments and the callback reads offsets.

### Save chunk pattern  <!-- id: save-chunk-pattern -->

1. `sub_XXXX_sizeof(void)` returns `sizeof(StructType)` — trivial.
2. `sub_XXXX_init(StructType *a0)` clears with `MI_CpuClear32`/`MI_CpuClear8` then sets defaults.
3. A getter calls `SaveArray_Get(saveData, SAVE_INDEX)` and returns the pointer; field getters/setters are trivial.
- `save_arrays.c` registers these via `DECL_CHUNK_EX` — replace the macro with an `#include` of the new header and remove the `DECL_CHUNK_EX` line. Check the index in `include/constants/save_arrays.h`.

### Overlay specifics  <!-- id: overlay-notes -->

- Overlay functions are named `ovNN_XXXXXXXX` (NN = overlay number, XXXXXXXX = address); overlay code loads at specific VMAs visible in labels.
- Overlay dependencies are declared in main.lsf (`After` clauses); each overlay has its own .sbin SHA1.

### Public vs static visibility  <!-- id: public-vs-static -->

Always check `asm/include/<file>.inc` `.public` declarations before marking functions static. Public functions must NOT be static (overlays call static-module functions by name → linker Undefined errors otherwise) and belong in `include/<file>.h`. The `.public` list mixes exports and imports — cross-reference with `thumb_func_start`/`arm_func_start` to split them.

### Enum casts required by -W noimplicitconv  <!-- id: enum-casts -->

MWCC rejects implicit int→enum conversions:
- `NarcId`: `GfGfxLoader_LoadCharData((NarcId)0x26, ...)`
- `GFPalSlotOffset`: cast computed expressions like `(enum GFPalSlotOffset)(palette_num << 5)`
- Any computed integer passed to an enum parameter needs an explicit cast.

### Save-chunk decomp IPA-safe: dedicated header, LEAVE save_arrays.c DECL_CHUNK_EX  <!-- id: save-chunk-ipa-safe -->

To decompile a save-chunk module (SaveArray_Get + MIi_CpuClear32, sizeof/init + field accessors) without IPA cascade: (1) put the struct + all prototypes in a NEW dedicated include/<name>.h that ONLY the new .c includes. (2) DO NOT modify save_arrays.c — leave its DECL_CHUNK_EX(sizefn, initfn) macro in place. Replacing the macro with #include <name>.h (the old pre-IPA-discipline move) recompiles save_arrays.c against a changed header set and IPA-cascades its codegen -> ROM mismatch. The DECL_CHUNK_EX extern decls and the new header decls coexist fine (separate TUs). sizeof fn: return sizeof(Struct); init: MI_CpuClear32(ptr, <sizeoffn>()) then set defaults; getter: return SaveArray_Get(saveData, SAVE_UNK_NN). Verify with chiri pkg -- compare (objdiff bl-placeholder diffs on the init are benign). Supersedes the earlier save-chunk-pattern that said to replace the macro.

## NONMATCHING Fallback

### NONMATCHING inline asm syntax (MWCC)  <!-- id: nonmatching-inline-asm-syntax -->

When using `asm void FuncName(...)`:
- `ldr rN, =0xVALUE` for literal-pool constants (NOT `ldr rN, label` + `label: .word`); `ldr rN, =FuncName` for function pointers.
- `bl FuncName` works directly; local labels (`_0201013A:`) work for branches.
- `.balign` directives are NOT supported — remove them.
- Wrap in `// clang-format off` / `// clang-format on`, and gate the C version with `#ifdef NONMATCHING`.

### MWCC collapses a deliberately-redundant double zero-load; NONMATCHING after a couple tries  <!-- id: redundant-double-zero-load-coalesce-wall -->

Some asm loads the SAME constant 0 into two registers (e.g. a byte-clear fill in caller-saved r1 + a separate i/state 0 in callee-saved r4), i.e. it is LESS optimal than necessary. Pure C re-converges: MWCC -O4 constant-coalesces the two zeros into one callee-saved register (the fill merges into i), producing one fewer movs -> a 2-byte SIZE diff. Source tricks that do NOT break the coalesce: block-scoping the clear, a named u8 fill var, tying state=i (manager->state = i; for(;i<2;i++)), C99 for-scoped i, do-while vs for. If you see a function that is identical except the asm has an extra movs #0 (redundant constant load) that your C optimizes away, do not burn many build cycles -- NONMATCHING that one function (asm static, keep C under ifdef NONMATCHING) and move on. Example: overlay_01_021FB4C0 ov01_021FB55C (struct byte-clear + slot-init).

## Tooling & Build Workflow

### objdiff.py usage and reliability  <!-- id: objdiff-usage -->

```bash
cp build/heartgold.us/asm/foo.o /tmp/foo_asm.o   # before flipping main.lsf
python3 tools/decomp_harness/objdiff.py /tmp/foo_asm.o build/heartgold.us/src/foo.o
python3 tools/decomp_harness/objdiff.py ... --summary      # also checks .rodata/.data/.bss
python3 tools/decomp_harness/objdiff.py ... --bytes sub_X  # per-function byte diff
```
- Plain function MATCH is based on **size**, not bytes — same-size functions with different registers report as MATCH. Verify critical functions with `--disasm FN`/`--bytes FN`.
- `--summary` checks data sections too; use it when pre-existing build errors block full-ROM `make compare`.

### Build workflow on macOS  <!-- id: build-macos -->

- Always `chiri pkg -- build` (or `-- compare`), never raw `make -C` — Wine CWD resolution breaks through symlinks and `.d` files get stale `Z:` paths (make spins at 100% CPU).
- Fast iteration: `chiri pkg -- build --target main --no-compare` (ARM9 only), then `chiri pkg -- compare`.
- Corrupted `.d` files: `find build -name "*.d" -delete` then `chiri pkg -- tidy` and rebuild.
- Prerequisites: `brew install gnu-sed arm-gcc-bin` (osx-cross/homebrew-arm tap).

### recomp.sh build recovery  <!-- id: recomp-tool -->

`./tools/decomp_harness/recomp.sh` handles build recovery: `--kill` (stale make/wine/mwcc), `--fix-d` (corrupted .d files), `--full` (clean rebuild), no args = kill + fix .d + tidy + rebuild main. Use when builds hang at 100% CPU, error after an asm→C switch in main.lsf, or won't restart after an interrupt.

### Verify a single object when the full build is blocked  <!-- id: single-object-build-escape -->

When an unrelated pre-existing error aborts make main (e.g. a dup-decl in a shared header), you can still compile+verify ONE file: cp the asm reference first (build/heartgold.us/asm/<name>.o to /tmp), switch main.lsf, then build just that object via the chiri make-target passthrough: chiri pkg -- build --no-compare -- build/heartgold.us/src/<name>.o (default --target all => empty make target, so the bare object path is the only thing built). Then objdiff.py --summary /tmp/<name>_asm.o build/heartgold.us/src/<name>.o. Isolates your file from the broken TU; gives function+data .o-level verification without the full ROM SHA1.

### objdiff bl-placeholder diffs are benign; chiri pkg -- compare is authoritative  <!-- id: objdiff-bl-placeholder-falsepos -->

objdiff.py can report DIFF on a function whose disassembly is byte-identical except the UNRELOCATED bl placeholder bytes: the assembler (mwasmarm) emits f7ff fffe for an external call, MWCC emits f000 f800. objdiff sees these as real halfword diffs (and may not pair them as bl-reloc diffs), but the linker overwrites both with the same relocated offset, so the final ROM is identical. Always confirm with chiri pkg -- compare (full ROM SHA1) before rejecting OR accepting: compare is the only authoritative test. objdiff also MISSES section-level diffs (alignment/padding/rodata). Use objdiff --disasm to confirm a flagged diff is only bl placeholders, then trust compare.

### Include NNS via global.h, never the leaf <nnsys/...> headers directly  <!-- id: nns-leaf-headers-via-global -->

NNS SDK leaf headers (e.g. <nnsys/g3d/binres/res_struct_accessor.h>, res_struct_accessor_inline.h, kernel.h, gfd VramMan types) do NOT include their own prerequisite type headers -> including them directly gives MWCC declaration syntax error (NNSG3dResMdlSet etc. undefined). The umbrella nnsys/g3d.h includes them in the correct dependency order, and global.h -> nitro/nnsys pulls the whole chain. Fix: rely on #include global.h for ALL NNS types AND inline accessors (NNS_G3dGetMdlByIdx, NNS_G3dGetResDataByIdx live in res_struct_accessor_inline.h which g3d.h includes). Do not add explicit <nnsys/...> includes; clang-format also sorts angle-bracket system includes to the TOP (above global.h), compounding the undefined-type failure. Example: unk_02069660.

### objdiff.py misreports SIZE/section for functions with inline Thumb jump-table data  <!-- id: objdiff-size-miscount-inline-jumptable -->

MWCC emits Thumb switch dispatch as `add r0,r0; add r0,pc; ldrh r0,[r0,#6]; lsl;asr; add pc,r0` followed by inline .short/.word offset-table data embedded in .text. objdiff.py's function-boundary/size heuristic can't tell this inline data from code, so it reports a spurious `SIZE N vs M` (often +8) for such functions and a small nonzero section-size delta — even when the bytes are IDENTICAL. The asm side disassembles the table as `.short`/`.word` (it has the source directives) while the C .o side shows the same bytes as bogus instructions (e.g. `movs r0,r1` = 0x0008). Verify with --disasm: if the instruction stream AND the table halfwords match (only bl relocs differ: asm fff7/feff vs c 00f0/00f8), the function matches. ALWAYS confirm with `chiri pkg -- compare` (authoritative) rather than trusting objdiff SIZE for jump-table functions. Seen in unk_02097BE0 (sub_02097BE0 5-case, sub_02097C50 4-case).

### When chiri compare fails but objdiff shows only jump-table SIZE mismatches, diff main.sbin built both ways  <!-- id: pinpoint-1byte-via-main-sbin-diff -->

For files full of inline-jump-table functions, objdiff reports SIZE mismatches for every function (it miscounts the inline .short tables) and refuses byte-level diffs, hiding any real 1-byte error. To pinpoint: build main with the C version (chiri pkg -- build --target main --no-compare) and `cp build/heartgold.us/main.sbin /tmp/main_c.sbin`; flip main.lsf back to the asm object, rebuild, `cp ... /tmp/main_asm.sbin`; then `cmp -l /tmp/main_asm.sbin /tmp/main_c.sbin` (asm baseline matches retail). cmp -l prints offsets+values in OCTAL and is 1-based. Convert: address = 0x02000000 + (byteno-1). `xxd -s <off> -l 48` both sbins to see context, then map to the function via the asm listing. This isolates a single differing byte (e.g. an asr-vs-lsr opcode) that objdiff masked. Used to find the lsr/asr bug in unk_0205BFF0 sub_0205C0A0.
